## EDA

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Load the data
df <- read_csv("W1_AvgSleepData.csv")

# Step 1: Remove 'SID' and 'c1remove'
sleep_vars <- names(df)[!names(df) %in% c("SID", "c1remove")]

# Step 2: Create a named list of interpretations
var_descriptions <- list(
  c1wakeall = "Average wake time across all days",
  c1wakeWE = "Average wake time on weekends",
  c1wakeWD = "Average wake time on weekdays",
  c1bedall = "Average bedtime across all days",
  c1bedWE = "Average bedtime on weekends",
  c1bedWD = "Average bedtime on weekdays",
  c1wakDif = "Difference in wake time (weekend - weekday)",
  c1bedDifMin = "Difference in bedtime (weekend - weekday)",
  c1TSTAl = "Total sleep time across all days (in minutes)",
  c1TSTWE = "Total sleep time on weekends (in minutes)",
  c1TSTWD = "Total sleep time on weekdays (in minutes)",
  c1TMIBWE = "Time in bed on weekends (in minutes)",
  c1TMIBALL = "Time in bed across all days (in minutes)",
  c1TMIBWD = "Time in bed on weekdays (in minutes)"
)

# Step 3: Plot each variable with interpretation as title
for (var in sleep_vars) {
  title_text <- if (!is.null(var_descriptions[[var]])) {
    paste0(var_descriptions[[var]], " (", var, ")")
  } else {
    paste("Sleep Variable", "(", var, ")")
  }
  
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[var]])) +
    geom_density(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.6) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = title_text, x = var, y = "Density")
  
  print(p)
}

```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Load the data
df <- read_csv("W1_AvgSleepData.csv")

# Select variables to test (excluding SID and c1remove)
test_vars <- names(df)[!names(df) %in% c("SID", "c1remove")]

# Run Shapiro-Wilk test on each variable and print results
for (var in test_vars) {
  values <- df[[var]]
  values <- values[!is.na(values)]  # Remove NAs
  
  if (length(values) >= 3 && length(values) <= 5000) {
    test_result <- shapiro.test(values)
    cat("\nVariable:", var, "\n",
        "W =", round(test_result$statistic, 4), 
        "| p-value =", format.pval(test_result$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("\nVariable:", var, "\n",
        "Shapiro-Wilk test skipped (requires 3-5000 non-NA values). Sample size:", length(values), "\n")
  }
}

```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(scales)

# Read and preprocess the data
df <- read_csv("W1_AvgSleepData.csv")

# Remove 'SID' and 'c1remove', scale the rest
scaled_df <- df %>%
  select(-SID, -c1remove) %>%
  scale()

# Compute correlation matrix
cor_mat <- cor(scaled_df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Convert to long format for ggplot
cor_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat))
colnames(cor_df) <- c("Var1", "Var2", "Correlation")

# Create the heatmap
ggplot(cor_df, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", 
                       midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1, 1), space = "Lab",
                       name = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank()) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Correlation Heatmap (Scaled Data)")

```

## Linear Models

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(randomForest)
library(tidyverse)

# Read data
df <- read.csv("W1_AvgSleepData.csv")

# Remove SID and c1remove
df <- df %>% select(-SID, -c1remove)

# Drop rows with any NA values
df_clean <- df %>% drop_na()

# Scale all columns
scaled_df <- scale(df_clean) %>% as.data.frame()

# Initialize result storage
results <- list()

# Loop through each column as target
for (target in colnames(scaled_df)) {
  
  predictors <- setdiff(colnames(scaled_df), target)
  
  # Create formula
  formula <- as.formula(paste(target, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = "+")))
  
  # Fit random forest
  rf_model <- randomForest(formula, data = scaled_df, importance = TRUE)
  
  # Get R-squared and importance
  rsq <- rf_model$rsq[length(rf_model$rsq)]
  importance_vals <- importance(rf_model)
  
  results[[target]] <- list(
    target = target,
    predictors = predictors,
    r_squared = rsq,
    importance = importance_vals
  )
}

# Summarize R-squared values
r_squared_summary <- tibble(
  Target = names(results),
  R_squared = sapply(results, function(x) x$r_squared)
)

# Display sorted by R² descending
print(r_squared_summary %>% arrange(desc(R_squared)))

```

```{r}
# Load plotting library
library(ggplot2)

# Create a folder to save plots (optional)
dir.create("feature_importance_plots", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Loop through each result and plot importance
for (res in results) {
  
  # Get importance data
  imp_df <- as.data.frame(res$importance)
  imp_df$Predictor <- rownames(imp_df)
  imp_df <- imp_df %>% 
    rename(Importance = `%IncMSE`) %>% 
    arrange(desc(Importance))
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(imp_df, aes(x = reorder(Predictor, Importance), y = Importance, fill = Importance)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "skyblue", high = "darkblue") +
    labs(title = paste("Feature Importance for Predicting", res$target),
         x = "Predictor",
         y = "% Increase in MSE when Removed") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
  
  # Print the plot (if in interactive mode)
  print(p)
  
  # Save each plot to disk
  ggsave(filename = paste0("feature_importance_plots/", res$target, "_importance.png"),
         plot = p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
}

```
